audit_phase: Phase 3.6 — Implementation Hardening, Metric Reconciliation & Production Validation
project: An AI-Driven DL–ML Integrated Framework for Crop Yield Prediction Using Environmental Factors

1_temporal_test_size.discrepancy: Temporal test size previously reported as 5,750 vs 4,534 rows.
1_temporal_test_size.source_investigation: Evaluated on clean deduplicated dataset (25,932 rows). For chronological boundary train <= 2008 and test >= 2009, exact counts are Train = 20,182 rows (77.8%), Test = 5,750 rows (22.2%). 4,534 was an ungrounded report entry (25,932 - 21,398).

2_geographic_test_size.discrepancy: Geographic test size previously reported as 5,197 rows across 16 unseen countries vs 4,376 rows across 20 unseen countries.
2_geographic_test_size.source_investigation: Evaluated using GroupKFold(n_splits=5) on Area. First fold yields exactly 16 held-out countries with 5,197 rows (20.04% of 25,932). 20 countries was a theoretical assumption (101 * 0.20 = 20.2), ignoring heterogeneous station counts per country.

3_base_training_group_count.discrepancy: Base-training group count reported as 6,564 vs 6,707.
3_base_training_group_count.source_investigation: Derived from 4-way disjoint group split. df_train_meta contains 8,534 unique groups. GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.2308, random_state=42) produces exactly 6,564 groups for Base and 1,970 groups for Meta. 6,707 was an unrounded theoretical estimate (8,534 - 1,827).

4_meta_training_group_count.discrepancy: Meta-training group count reported as 1,970 vs 1,827.
4_meta_training_group_count.source_investigation: As proven above, GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.2308, random_state=42) on df_train_meta (8,534 groups) partitions exactly 1,970 groups into Meta-Training. 6,564 + 1,970 = 8,534. Sum across all 4 sets: 6,564 (Base) + 1,970 (Meta) + 1,970 (Calib) + 2,626 (Test) = 13,130 unique groups.

5_stacking_r2_naive_random_split.discrepancy: Stacking R2 reported as 0.9815 vs 0.9822 on naive random split.
5_stacking_r2_naive_random_split.source_investigation: Both represent the 4-model DL–ML Stacking Meta-Ensemble evaluated on the exact same 80/20 naive random split (5,187 test rows). The 0.0007 difference stems from non-deterministic CPU floating-point accumulation in PyTorch Tabular Neural Network backpropagation across runs. Crucially, both are inflated by 58.67% test row repeated-tuple leakage. True leakage-aware grouped generalization is R2 = 0.9671.

grouped_leakage_aware_split.honesty_declaration: Random Forest (R2=0.9689, RMSE=1.448 t/ha) slightly outperforms Stacking (R2=0.9671, RMSE=1.490 t/ha) on the leakage-aware grouped split. Stacking does NOT outperform every baseline under zero-leakage evaluation.

phase4_conformal_calibration_audit.bounds_strict_ordering: lower = max(0.0, y_hat - Q), upper = max(lower, y_hat + Q) verified
